cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae, and he just told them, "And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him." WHATEVER you do, friend, and that covers stamping cookies, answering emails, even sitting in traffic yelling at nobody. Now he goes through a household, one person at a time.
First up, the wives. Paul writes, "Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord."

cards.question: Next, Paul turns to the husbands. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Love your wives and do not be harsh
Lead your wives and guard your home
Provide for your wives and keep the peace

cards.text: Then Paul talks to the children. He tells them to obey their parents in everything.

cards.question: Paul says children should obey their parents because it pleases the Lord.
Paul tells fathers not to provoke their children, so the children won't become ___.

cards.text: Next, Paul speaks to slaves. He tells them to obey their earthly masters in everything.

cards.question: Paul says slaves shouldn't obey only to please their masters at certain times. Which times?

answers.text: When the masters give a reward
When the masters are in a good mood

cards.question: Paul wants their obedience to come from sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul says whatever you do, work at it with your whole being. Your WHOLE being, friend, not just the half that hit snooze three times and is still negotiating with the pillow.

cards.question: Paul says to work as for the ___ and not for ___.
Paul says they will receive something from the Lord as their reward. What is it?
Paul says that in the end, it's their earthly masters they are really serving.
Paul says that when it comes to repaying wrong, some people get favoritism.

cards.text: Now Paul turns to the masters. He tells them to supply their slaves with what is right and fair.

cards.question: Paul tells the masters to treat their slaves with what is right and fair. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They also have a Master in heaven
Their slaves will serve them better
They will be repaid with honor

cards.text: Paul is still writing to the believers in Colossae, and now he moves from the household to prayer. He tells them to devote themselves to prayer and to stay watchful.

cards.question: Paul wants them devoted to prayer, both watchful and ___.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them to pray for us too. And he mentions, almost in passing, that he is in chains.

cards.question: Paul is in chains, and he asks them to pray that God will open something for us. What?
Paul says he is in chains for the mystery of Christ.

cards.text: The man is in chains, and the door he asks prayer for is a door for the word. Me? Years in a junk drawer, and the only door I EVER cared about was the DRAWER.

cards.question: Paul asks them to pray that he may declare the message ___, as he should.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to how the believers act toward outsiders.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to stay away from outsiders.

cards.text: Paul says act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time. I spent YEARS in a drawer counting falling dust, friend, so trust me, I'm a big fan of redeeming the time.

Then Paul gets to how they talk: always gracious, seasoned with salt. Seasoned, friend, not SALTY, and there's a big difference between a pinch of salt and the coworker who hits reply-all at midnight.

cards.question: Paul wants their speech always gracious and seasoned with salt. Why?

answers.text: So they know how to answer everyone
So they can win every argument
So people will speak well of them

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time without being introduced (for example, as an apostle). The card also states that he is writing to the believers in Colossae, which comes from Colossians 1:1-2, but it cites only Colossians 3:17.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The fact that Paul wrote the letter to Colossae comes from outside the passage, but its reference (Colossians 1:1-2) isn't given.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop are bare restatements with no Papa Dorin voice. Card 2 is just the verse, and cards 4, 7 and 15 each give a single flat sentence. The only voiced cards are cards 1 and 10.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says "their obedience" without saying whose. The slaves were named on earlier cards, and those cards are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Lord" is the only capitalized word among the five options, so it stands out as a right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "praise" (not for praise) is close in meaning to the right answer "men" (not for men, that is, not for people's approval). A baker could argue that it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The blanks ask the baker to supply the remaining words of verse 23's line ("as for the Lord and not for men"), which is a guess at the wording rather than a test of its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question says "they will receive" without saying who "they" are, and that context is on cards the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Paul's request is paraphrased in his own voice as "pray for us too" without quotation marks and without saying who "us" is. In Papa Dorin's mouth, "us" reads as Papa Dorin and the baker.

rule.text: Who's speaking. When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The question asks what God will open "for us" without saying who "us" is (Paul and those with him).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The card repeats what cards 3 to 5 already covered (Paul is in chains, and he asks for a door for the word) and adds no new part of the passage. It is a recap card that carries a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the core action. The verse contrasts gracious speech with harsh speech, but "the coworker who hits reply-all at midnight" is about bad timing and spamming people, not about being salty or harsh, so the joke doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
